courses.title: General Chemistry for Engineers
courses.description: Provides engineering students with a background in pertinent concepts and principles of chemistry. Topics include atomic theory of structure and bonding, stoichiometry, gases, equilibrium, oxidation-reduction, electrochemistry, thermodynamics, and reaction kinetics, and their applications to engineering.
courses.prerequisites: C or better MAT 105, MAT 106, MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 120, MAT 125, MAT 130, MAT 191, MAT 214, MAT 216, MAT 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, STA 1200 , SAT Math>=550, or ACT Math>=23.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: [GE 5A] Fundamental principles and concepts of chemistry, including atomic and molecular structure; nomenclature; stoichiometry; solution chemistry, including acid-base and redox chemistry; quantum theory; periodic properties; bonding theory; thermochemistry; gases; and intermolecular forces. Corequisite(s): CHM 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: SAT Math>=550; ACT Math>=23; ALEKS >=76; C or better in MAT 12, 105, 106, 112, 114, 115, 116, 120, 125, 130, 191, 214, 216, 224, MAT 1050 , MAT 1052 , MAT 1060 , MAT 1070 , MAT 1140 , MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , MAT 1250 , MAT 1300 , MAT 1310 , MAT 1910 , MAT 2140 , MAT 2240 , MAT 2250 , STA 120, or STA 1200 ; or C- or better in CHM 121 and CHM 121L.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You
courses.description: The development of the individual in society from an engineering perspective. The study of the integration of society and technology. Development includes introduction to the fields of engineering and engineering technology, career planning, development of a community of learners, critical thinking, problem solving skills, and ethical and professional behavior. Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Engineering, Society, and You Laboratory

Analysis of typical problems involving technology in society and their solutions. Guest speakers. Exposure to campus resources and provides a framework for developing and implementing an academic plan culminating in the award of a four-year degree.

courses.title: Project Design Principles and Applications
courses.description: [GE 5D] Selection and completion of scientific/technological synthesis application project under faculty supervision. Multidisciplinary team project. Projects that students solve in discipline of practice. Both formal written and oral reports.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: C/C++ Programming
courses.description: Introduction to structured programming using C/C++. Programming problems applicable to engineering technology. Control structures, Loops, Arrays, Pointers, Classes, Data structures, Data abstraction, Overloading, Templates, Files and Streams. 3 hours lecture/problem-solving. Corequisite(s): ETE 1151L .
courses.prerequisites: ESET, ETT, or EMSET major; and MAT 1060 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1310 .

courses.title: C/C++ Programming Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to C/C++ Programming. Writing programs using control structures, loops, functions, arrays, pointers, classes and inheritance. Corequisite(s): ETE 1151 .
courses.prerequisites: ESET, ETT, or EMSET major; and MAT 1060 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1310 .

courses.title: Electrical Networks
courses.description: Introduction to DC and AC circuit theory and applications. Electrical circuit analysis and electrical measurement involving RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Characteristics and applications of passive filters. Introduction to AC circuit applications including transformers and Three Phase Power. Corequisite(s): ETE 2011L .
courses.prerequisites: EMSET major; MAT 1060 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1310 ; PHY 1220 ; and PHY 1220L . (Not open to ESET major).

courses.title: Electrical Networks Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to DC and AC circuit theory and applications. Electrical circuit analysis and electrical measurement involving RC, RL, and RLC circuits. Characteristics and applications of passive filters. Transformers and Three Phase Circuit Applications. Not open to ESET majors. Corequisite(s): ETE 2011 .
courses.prerequisites: EMSET major; MAT 1060 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1310 ; PHY 1220 ; and PHY 1220L . (Not open to ESET major).

courses.title: Electronic Systems
courses.description: Introduction to semiconductor devices and circuits including diode, transistor, and active amplifiers. Study of electrical and electronic systems involving motors, oscillators, sensors, optoelectronic devices, and PLCs. 3 hours lectures/problem-solving. Corequisite(s): ETE 3211L .
courses.prerequisites: ETT or EMSET major; MAT 1300 or MAT 130; and C- or better in ETE 2011 or ETT 201, and ETE 2011L or ETT 201L. (Not open to ECET or ESET major).

courses.title: Electronic Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to semiconductor devices and circuits including diode, transistor, and active amplifiers. Study of electrical and electronic systems involving motors, oscillators, sensors, optoelectronic devices, and PLC. 1 three hour laboratory. Corequisite(s): ETE 3211 .
courses.prerequisites: ETT or EMSET major; MAT 1300 or MAT 130; and C- or better in ETE 2011 or ETT 201, and ETE 2011L or ETT 201L. (Not open to ECET or ESET major).

Ethical Concepts in Technology and Applied Science
courses.description: [GE 3C or 5D] Explores ethics of engineers, scientists, and others involved with technology related to values, philosophy, ethical theory and practice, moral reasoning, morality in law and codes, professional standards, and societies-case studies. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.

courses.title: Technical Calculus I
courses.description: [GE 2] Differential and integral calculus of polynomial, rational, trigonometric, logarithmic and exponential functions, with applications of the derivative and the integral.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1050 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1052 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1055 and MAT 1060 ; C or better in MAT 1070 ; AP PreCalculus >=3; or ALEKS Comp >=76.

courses.title: Technical Calculus II
courses.description: Infinite series, an introduction to ordinary differential equations and Laplace transforms.
courses.prerequisites: C or better in MAT 1150 , MAT 1300 , or MAT 1300B.

courses.title: Engineering Graphics I
courses.description: Engineering graphics for product design, manufacturing and construction. Emphasis on graphic communication used for processing parts and layouts. Orthographic projection, pictorial views, section and auxiliary views, dimensioning for production-processing, and the four fundamental views of descriptive geometry. Use of instruments and CAD for engineering drawings. Corequisite(s): MFE 1260L .

courses.title: Engineering Graphics I Laboratory
courses.description: Engineering graphics for product design, manufacturing and construction. Emphasis on graphic communication used for processing parts and layouts. Orthographic projection, pictorial views, section and auxiliary views, dimensioning for production-processing, and the four fundamental views of descriptive geometry. Use of instruments and CAD for engineering drawings Corequisite(s): MFE 1260 .

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010L .

courses.title: Manufacturing Systems and Processes Laboratory
courses.description: Study of basic manufacturing processes with emphasis on terminology, technology, process principles and capabilities, material selection and comparative advantages and disadvantages. Processes discussed include material removal, joining, assembly, 3D printing and casting. Other topics include NC, measurement and gaging, and statistical methods. Corequisite(s): MFE 2010 .

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat
courses.description: [GE 5A] Introduction to Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics: Kinematics, forces, conservation laws, viscous fluids, heat transfer, and the microscopic nature of gases. Emphasis on biological applications. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in MAT 106, MAT 1060 , MAT 112, MAT 114, MAT 1140 , MAT 1140C, MAT 115, MAT 116, MAT 1150 , MAT 1200 , or MAT 1300 . ( MAT 1300 can be concurrent.)

courses.title: Physics of Motion, Fluids, and Heat Laboratory
courses.description: [GE 5C] Experiments on Newtonian mechanics, fluids, and heat. Corequisite(s): PHY 1210 .

courses.title: Physics of Electromagnetism, Circuits, and Light
courses.description: Electric and magnetic forces and fields, DC and AC circuits, oscillations, electromagnetic waves, optics, and analogies between diffusion and electrostatics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1220L .
courses.prerequisites: C- or better in PHY 122, PHY 122B, PHY 1210 , or PHY 1210B.

courses.title: Electromagnetism, Circuits, and Light Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments on electromagnetism, oscillations, and optics. Corequisite(s): PHY 1220 .
